-81.59070,30.25770.name: Advanced Reproductive Specialists, Jacksonville Center for Reproductive Medicine
-81.59070,30.25770.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Michael D. Fox, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

72.80990,21.15977.name: Shree Shubh Hospital and Infertility clinic
72.80990,21.15977.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-59.58910,13.27707.name: Barbados Primate Research Center (BPRC)
-59.58910,13.27707.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.26398,51.33185.name: NewLife Fertility Centre
-0.26398,51.33185.state: The Pines, 2 The Parade, Epsom, Surrey, KT18 5DH, United Kingdom
-0.26398,51.33185.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-120.36403,50.67245.name: Thompson Rivers University
-120.36403,50.67245.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, September 2025
-120.36403,50.67245.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, September 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-122.29000,37.86000.name: Ansa Biotechnologies
-122.29000,37.86000.desc: Uses enzymatic synthesis to build unusually long DNA sequences, holding records for single-run length. Longer synthetic constructs mean whole genes and eventually whole genomes can be ordered rather than assembled, which changes what a screening system has to recognise.

109.16700,18.30700.name: Yazhou Bay Seed Laboratory, Hainan
109.16700,18.30700.state: Sanya, Hainan — Yazhou Bay Science and Technology City
109.16700,18.30700.desc: A state seed-breeding complex on Hainan, where the climate allows several generations a year and where much of China's crop breeding is accelerated. Concentrating national breeding capacity in one place is a deliberate industrial policy, and there is no equivalent elsewhere.

20.26300,63.82580.name: SweTree Technologies
20.26300,63.82580.desc: A forest biotechnology company founded in 1999, owned by the forestry industry it serves — its main shareholders include three of Sweden's largest forest companies alongside a research holding vehicle. It holds first right of refusal on innovations from a company assembling around forty senior Swedish researchers, and works with the Umeå Plant Science Centre. Its core work is not transgenes: it is somatic embryogenesis, in which one seed is made to yield many embryos, so an elite tree can be copied at industrial scale. A pilot plant producing about 100,000 spruce seedlings a year is intended to become a factory at 20 million, co-owned by the same forest companies. That is clonal forestry rather than genetic engineering, and it raises the question this facet keeps circling: twenty million copies of a selected genotype is a narrowing of a forest's genetic base whether or not a single gene was inserted.
